messages.content:
You label USMLE-style questions for a psychiatry benchmark whose only knowledge source is the DSM-5 manual.

Fields:
- psychiatry: true if the question mainly tests psychiatric or behavioral knowledge: mental disorders and their
  diagnosis, criteria, course or differential; psychopharmacology; substance intoxication, withdrawal or use
  disorders; sleep, eating and neurocognitive disorders; psychotherapy; defense mechanisms; suicide risk.
  False when psychiatric words are incidental (e.g. "ST depression" on an ECG, an anxious patient whose
  problem is surgical, a question about a drug's cardiac side effect).
- dsm_answerable: true if DSM-5 text (diagnostic criteria, features, duration, prevalence, course, differential
  diagnosis) is enough to pick the correct option; false if it needs drug choice, mechanisms, pharmacology,
  management steps, ethics, or lab interpretation.
- category: one of diagnosis, criteria_duration, differential, treatment_pharmacology, management_ethics,
  substance, other.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"psychiatry": true or false, "dsm_answerable": true or false, "category": "...", "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
A 20-year-old college student is brought to his primary care physician by his parents over the New Years holiday because they are concerned about his behavior since right after high school graduation in May the spring before. Prior to this year, he was generally an outgoing and social young man, who now reportedly has been spending the majority of his time alone in his dorm room and room at home, where his mother and father have overheard him talking to other people when he has no guests. When asked if anything was bothering him at school, he reports that at night the voice of the school's mascot encourages him to save the school from the large oak grove that will soon takeover the student union building by setting the trees on fire for all to see. On exam, his appears to be otherwise healthy and his urine toxicology screen is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. Schizoaffective disorder
B. Major depression
C. Schizophrenia
D. Schizophreniform disorder
E. Malingering

Correct answer: C. Schizophrenia

text: {"psychiatry": true, "dsm_answerable": true, "category": "diagnosis", "reason": "Tests DSM-5 duration criterion distinguishing schizophrenia (>6 months of symptoms) from schizophreniform disorder in a psychotic patient."}
